+# Real Heat of the Actual Centered Boundary Operator
+
+## Abstract
+
+The original real centered boundary space G0 carries a spectral heat semigroup whose generator is exactly minus the original boundary operator on its entire centered domain.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The Real Heat Multiplier).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryHeat.heat`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryHeat.heat` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For a real Hilbert basis e of the original G0 and positive covariance eigenvalues mu, heat(e,mu,t) transports the bounded coordinate multipliers exp(-t/mu(i)) through e.repr. Time t is nonnegative. The map acts on every vector of G0; it does not replace that space by finite sequences.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (The Ambient Heat).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryHeat.fullHeat`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryHeat.fullHeat` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+On the original ambient G, fullHeat fixes constG(mean(F)) and applies centered heat to the orthogonal centered part Pi(F), included isometrically back into G. It uses the original real carriers and the same covariance sequence.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (The Actual Heat, Trace and Generator).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryHeat.actual_heat`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Arith/FibonacciAtomic/Geometry/BiasedBoundaryHeat.actual_heat` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+One application of the actual spectral counting theorem supplies paired bases e on G0 and k on the effective edge space K, together with one positive nonincreasing covariance sequence mu tending to zero. The original Sigma and ambient C have their actual paired diagonal actions on this same family. The original source centeredTrace with codomain G0 has the same paired action before inclusion. Its composition with the actual isometric inclusion G0 into G equals ambient C, and centeredTrace adjoint composed with centeredTrace is literally Sigma on the entire original edge carrier. Every repeated eigenvalue keeps its own basis occurrence.
+
+The transported heat operators form a strongly continuous contraction semigroup. They are positive, and their intrinsic extended positive trace is the sum of ofReal(exp(-t/mu(i))) for every nonnegative t. The formula also holds at time zero as an extended value. At every positive time the series is summable and the intrinsic positive trace is finite. The real trace value is the toReal of this proved finite extended trace.
+
+For all centered vectors u and v, the strong limit at time zero from the right of t inverse times (S(t)u-u) equals v if and only if (u,-v) lies in the original boundaryOperator graph after the original isometric inclusion into G. The parameterized polar graph and coefficient identities apply to the same e,k,mu and give the exact all-vector coefficient graph. Continuous coefficient functionals prove one direction. Finite basis projections of both the vector and its original graph image, followed by the real semigroup generator-limit theorem, prove the reverse direction.
+
+Any other strongly continuous contraction semigroup with this same full generator graph equals S. The multiplier, finite-span continuity and uniqueness design reuse the standard construction in DiagonalHeat and the attributed MarkovProcess supplies in ContractionSemigroup. No self-adjoint realization, inverse-domain, spectral exhaustion or counting proof is repeated.
+
+The ambient heat is also a strongly continuous positive contraction semigroup, with the strong generator equal to minus the original boundaryOperator on every vector in its exact domain. It uniquely has that generator. Its restriction to the original G0 is the centered heat, and it fixes every original constant. A complete orthonormal basis consisting of constG(1) and the included centered basis proves that its intrinsic trace is exactly one plus the centered trace, with exactly one added constant mode.
+
+For every s>0 the centered trace lies between (b/s) exp(-s/b) and B/s, with b=phi to the power minus two and B=2 phi cubed. When 0<s<=b, its lower bound is b/(exp(1) s), including equality in the time cutoff. The proof compares the same ordered reciprocal eigenvalues with shifted geometric exponentials. Their summability is established before using real infinite sums or the toReal trace.
+
+The inclusive finite cutoff count equals the sum of inclusive mode indicators, counting every repeated occurrence. The Laplace identity is proved with the original positiveCount: the centered trace is s times the integral on u>0 of exp(-s u) Nplus(u). Each indicator tail is integrable; the norms of their integrals have a summable series. Interchanging sum and integral is therefore justified, and the closed tail endpoint has zero Lebesgue measure.
+
+The logarithm of the inclusive positive count divided by log(lambda) tends to one at infinity. The logarithm of the original one-based eigenvalue divided by log(j) also tends to one. The centered and ambient heat logarithms divided by log(1/s) tend to one from positive times at zero. The proof squeezes each quotient between positive constant multiples with the same diverging logarithmic denominator. It asserts no Weyl coefficient or additive counting remainder.
+
+The separate operator approximation-number/singular-value correspondence, Schatten classes and equivalence of finite intrinsic positive trace with trace class remain open. The heat and intrinsic-trace statements therefore do not establish the full original Theorem 3.1 or its covariance ideal corollary. Sigma, rather than C, is the object of the source Hilbert-Schmidt assertion. The original C has centered codomain G0. Its precise ambient inclusion and Gram equality are proved here; the full-carrier singular-value correspondence remains open.
+

+# Intrinsic Positive Trace on Real Hilbert Spaces
+
+## Abstract
+
+The positive trace is an extended nonnegative quantity defined from the operator by all finite orthonormal test families. The definition chooses no basis or scalar spectrum and permits an infinite value.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Positive Trace).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/HilbertOperators/RealPositiveTrace.positiveTrace`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/HilbertOperators/RealPositiveTrace.positiveTrace` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For a bounded real linear operator A, positiveTrace(A) is the supremum, over every natural n and every orthonormal family v indexed by Fin n, of the sum of ofReal(inner(v(j),A(v(j)))). Its intended use is for positive operators. Neither compactness nor summability is required to define this extended value.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Complete Positive Diagonal).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/HilbertOperators/RealPositiveTrace.positive_trace_diagonal`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/HilbertOperators/RealPositiveTrace.positive_trace_diagonal` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let e be a complete real Hilbert basis of E and let A be a continuous real linear operator on that same carrier. Suppose d(i) is nonnegative and, for every vector x and every index i, the i-th coefficient of A(x) is d(i) times the i-th coefficient of x. Then A is positive and its intrinsic positive trace is the extended sum of ofReal(d(i)). The index type can be empty, finite or infinite, and the trace can be infinite.
+
+Parseval gives the convergent quadratic-form series for each test vector. Interchanging nonnegative extended sums and applying finite-family Bessel bounds each finite orthonormal trace sum by the diagonal sum. Conversely, every finite selection of the supplied eigenvectors is an admissible test family. Taking the supremum of those finite selections gives the reverse inequality. Thus two complete positive diagonal presentations yield the same value because each equals the same operator-defined supremum.
+
+This is the standard finite-family construction of positive trace. It supplies the original real boundary heat with an intrinsic operator trace without a complexification, a finite-dimensional algebraic trace, or a scalar sequence used as the definition of trace. The separate identification with singular-value trace class is an additional mathematical statement.
+

+private theorem exponential_series (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) :
+    HasSum (fun n : ℕ => Real.exp (-x * ((n : ℝ)+1)))
+      (Real.exp (-x) / (1-Real.exp (-x))) := by
+  have hq : Real.exp (-x) < 1 := Real.exp_lt_one_iff.mpr (neg_neg_of_pos hx)
+  convert (hasSum_geometric_of_lt_one (Real.exp_pos (-x)).le hq).mul_left
+    (Real.exp (-x)) using 1

+private theorem exponential_series_bounds (x : ℝ) (hx : 0 < x) :

+  have hq1 : Real.exp (-x) < 1 := Real.exp_lt_one_iff.mpr (neg_neg_of_pos hx)

+  constructor
+  · apply (div_le_div_iff₀ hx hd).mpr
+    have he := Real.add_one_le_exp (-x)
+    nlinarith [mul_nonneg hq.le (show 0 ≤ x-(1-Real.exp (-x)) by linarith)]
+  · apply (div_le_div_iff₀ hd hx).mpr
+    have he := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (Real.add_one_le_exp x) hq.le
+    have hid : Real.exp x * Real.exp (-x) = 1 := by rw [← Real.exp_add]; simp
+    rw [hid] at he
+    nlinarith

+private theorem heat_estimates (e : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ G0) (mu : ℕ → ℝ)
+    (hp : ∀ i, 0 < mu i)
+    (hl : ∀ i : ℕ, ((i : ℝ)+1)/BiasedBoundaryCounting.B ≤ (mu i)⁻¹)
+    (hu : ∀ i, (mu i)⁻¹ ≤ ((i : ℝ)+1)/BiasedBoundaryTrace.b)
+    (t : ℝ≥0) (ht : 0 < t) :
+    Summable (fun i => Real.exp (-(t : ℝ)*(mu i)⁻¹)) ∧
+    positiveTrace (heat e mu hp t) < ⊤ ∧
+    (BiasedBoundaryTrace.b/(t : ℝ))*Real.exp (-(t : ℝ)/BiasedBoundaryTrace.b) ≤
+      (positiveTrace (heat e mu hp t)).toReal ∧
+    (positiveTrace (heat e mu hp t)).toReal ≤ BiasedBoundaryCounting.B/(t : ℝ) ∧
+    ((t : ℝ) ≤ BiasedBoundaryTrace.b →
+      BiasedBoundaryTrace.b/(Real.exp 1*(t : ℝ)) ≤
+        (positiveTrace (heat e mu hp t)).toReal) := by
+  let b := BiasedBoundaryTrace.b
+  let B := BiasedBoundaryCounting.B
+  have hb : 0 < b := pow_pos BiasedBoundaryTrace.a_pos 2
+  have hB : 0 < B := div_pos (mul_pos (by norm_num) Real.goldenRatio_pos) hb
+  have htR : 0 < (t : ℝ) := ht
+  have hL := exponential_series ((t : ℝ)/b) (div_pos htR hb)
+  have hU := exponential_series ((t : ℝ)/B) (div_pos htR hB)
+  have hle (i : ℕ) : Real.exp (-((t : ℝ)/b)*((i : ℝ)+1)) ≤
+      Real.exp (-(t : ℝ)*(mu i)⁻¹) := by
+    apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
+    have hi := mul_le_mul_of_nonpos_left (hu i) (neg_nonpos.mpr t.coe_nonneg)
+    convert hi using 1 <;> ring
+  have hge (i : ℕ) : Real.exp (-(t : ℝ)*(mu i)⁻¹) ≤
+      Real.exp (-((t : ℝ)/B)*((i : ℝ)+1)) := by
+    apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
+    have hi := mul_le_mul_of_nonpos_left (hl i) (neg_nonpos.mpr t.coe_nonneg)
+    convert hi using 1 <;> ring
+  have hs : Summable (fun i => Real.exp (-(t : ℝ)*(mu i)⁻¹)) :=
+    hU.summable.of_nonneg_of_le (fun i => (Real.exp_pos _).le) hge
+  have htr := (positive_trace_diagonal e (heat e mu hp t) _
+    (fun i => (Real.exp_pos _).le) (heat_coeff e mu hp t)).2
+  have hreal : (positiveTrace (heat e mu hp t)).toReal =
+      ∑' i, Real.exp (-(t : ℝ)*(mu i)⁻¹) := by
+    rw [htr, ← ENNReal.ofReal_tsum_of_nonneg (fun i => (Real.exp_pos _).le) hs,
+      ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (tsum_nonneg fun i => (Real.exp_pos _).le)]
+  have hlo := (exponential_series_bounds ((t : ℝ)/b) (div_pos htR hb)).1.trans
+    (hL.tsum_eq ▸ hL.summable.tsum_le_tsum hle hs)
+  have hup := (hU.tsum_eq ▸ hs.tsum_le_tsum hge hU.summable).trans
+    (exponential_series_bounds ((t : ℝ)/B) (div_pos htR hB)).2
+  have hlow : (b/(t : ℝ))*Real.exp (-(t : ℝ)/b) ≤
+      (positiveTrace (heat e mu hp t)).toReal := by
+    have hid : (b/(t : ℝ))*Real.exp (-(t : ℝ)/b) =
+        Real.exp (-((t : ℝ)/b))/((t : ℝ)/b) := by
+      rw [show -(t : ℝ)/b = -((t : ℝ)/b) by ring]
+      field_simp
+    rw [hreal,hid]
+    exact hlo
+  refine ⟨hs,htr ▸ hs.tsum_ofReal_lt_top,hlow,?_,?_⟩
+  · change (positiveTrace (heat e mu hp t)).toReal ≤ B/(t : ℝ)
+    rw [hreal]
+    simpa only [one_div_div] using hup
+  · intro htb
+    have hratio : (t : ℝ)/b ≤ 1 := (div_le_one hb).mpr htb
+    have he : (Real.exp 1)⁻¹ ≤ Real.exp (-(t : ℝ)/b) := by
+      rw [← Real.exp_neg]
+      apply Real.exp_le_exp.mpr
+      simpa only [neg_div] using neg_le_neg hratio
+    have hm := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left he (div_pos hb htR).le
+    have heq : b/(Real.exp 1*(t : ℝ)) = (b/(t : ℝ))*(Real.exp 1)⁻¹ := by ring
+    rw [heq]
+    exact hm.trans hlow

+private theorem log_growth {α : Type*} (l : Filter α) (x y : α → ℝ)
+    (hx : Tendsto x l atTop) (a c : ℝ) (ha : 0 < a) (hc : 0 < c)
+    (hbound : ∀ᶠ t in l, a*x t ≤ y t ∧ y t ≤ c*x t) :
+    Tendsto (fun t => Real.log (y t)/Real.log (x t)) l (𝓝 1) := by
+  have hlog := Real.tendsto_log_atTop.comp hx
+  have hscale (b : ℝ) (hb : 0 < b) :
+      Tendsto (fun t => Real.log (b*x t)/Real.log (x t)) l (𝓝 1) := by
+    have hlim := ((tendsto_const_nhds (x := Real.log b)).div_atTop hlog).add_const 1
+    simp only [zero_add] at hlim
+    apply hlim.congr'
+    filter_upwards [hx.eventually_gt_atTop 1] with t ht
+    have hp : 0 < x t := lt_trans zero_lt_one ht
+    rw [Real.log_mul hb.ne' hp.ne',add_div,div_self (Real.log_pos ht).ne']
+    rfl
+  apply (hscale a ha).squeeze' (hscale c hc)
+  · filter_upwards [hbound,hx.eventually_gt_atTop 1] with t ht hx1
+    exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right
+      (Real.log_le_log (mul_pos ha (lt_trans zero_lt_one hx1)) ht.1) (Real.log_pos hx1).le
+  · filter_upwards [hbound,hx.eventually_gt_atTop 1] with t ht hx1
+    have hy := (mul_pos ha (lt_trans zero_lt_one hx1)).trans_le ht.1
+    exact div_le_div_of_nonneg_right (Real.log_le_log hy ht.2) (Real.log_pos hx1).le

+private theorem heat_log_limits (e : HilbertBasis ℕ ℝ G0) (mu : ℕ → ℝ)

+    (hl : ∀ i : ℕ, ((i : ℝ)+1)/BiasedBoundaryCounting.B ≤ (mu i)⁻¹)

+    · convert h.2.2.2.1 using 1 <;> ring
+  constructor
